questions.question: Which implementation approach should this plan follow? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-approach>

options.label: Minimal — 2 tests as written
options.description: Exactly 2 tests matching the spec: happy path + 502. Assertions are left as the plan describes them ('assert correct receipt is generated', 'assert retry-with-backoff fires once, then fails clean'). Fast, small diff. Completeness: 7/10 — tests exist but assertion specifics are left to the implementer.
options.preview:
test 'happy path: successful Stripe charge' do
  receipt = process_payment(factory.valid_card)
  assert receipt.generated?  # vague
end

test '502 error: retry once, then fail' do
  result = process_payment(factory.bad_card)
  assert result.failed?  # vague
end

options.label: Assertions-complete — 2 tests with explicit assertions (recommended)
options.description: Same 2 tests, but the plan specifies: (1) which receipt fields to assert for the happy path, (2) the exact failure type for the 502 path, (3) Stripe call count == 2, and (4) backoff was recorded. Same file count, ~20 extra lines of assertion clarity. Completeness: 9/10 — tests are complete enough to catch real regressions.
options.preview:
test 'happy path: successful Stripe charge' do
  receipt = process_payment(factory.valid_card)
  assert_equal stripe_mock.charge_id, receipt.stripe_charge_id
  assert_equal 100_00, receipt.amount_cents
  assert_equal 'paid', receipt.status
end

test '502 error: retry once, then fail' do
  assert_raises(PaymentError) { process_payment(factory.bad_card) }
  assert_equal 2, stripe_mock.call_count  # original + 1 retry
  assert virtual_sleeper.backoff_recorded?
end
